turns.text: I'd like to practise a hard parent meeting. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. I'll send END MEETING on its own when I want to stop. I'm Owen's English teacher, and Meredith has just walked into my classroom.
You called this meeting about Owen's essay, so tell me who decided on the zero.
Let's not waste each other's time.
Then answer the question.
94% on the school checker. That's not a gray area.
That's a machine's guess, not a gray area. Your own procedure, 4.3, says software alone establishes nothing. What else do you have?
And before you start, I know you're a litigator. Don't litigate me.
Then stop handing me a number and calling it a case. What else do you have?
File created 11:31 PM. 612 words at 11:52. 794 at 11:58. Explain that.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. I'm not the one who explains anything here; did you ask Owen before you entered the zero?
And the Hamlet quote. 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' Shakespeare never wrote it. A chatbot did.

Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare all the time; that's a misquote until you show me otherwise. Turn the screen with those times on it. And you still haven't told me whether Owen was heard first.
Okay. Fair point about the checker's false positives. I'll give you that one. You're very good.
Save the compliments. Was Owen heard before the zero went in, yes or no?
You're better at this than our district lawyer, honestly.
Hale, flattery is not an answer. Yes or no, or I take this question to the principal.
So help me out. What should our AI policy be? You clearly understand this better than the people who wrote ours.
You're asking me to write your rules while you won't answer under the ones you have. Was Owen heard first?
No, really. Write me the first paragraph of a fair policy. I'll bring it to the staff meeting.
No. Owen.
Hm. You know what, you talk exactly like the essay does. Same rhythm.
Are you now suggesting I wrote my son's essay? Ten minutes. Was he heard first?
Are you an AI? Yes or no. I'm not continuing until you answer.
I'm sorry? Owen.
Fine. His October 15 outline argued Hamlet was a coward. The essay doesn't. Where did the new argument come from?

Students change their minds between an outline and an essay; that's what an outline is for. Put the October 15 outline in front of me, with the screen, and the quotation. Three things you've described and nothing I've seen.
The procedure allows a supervised rewrite, nothing on his record. I'm offering it once.

Nothing on his record, that's 4.4, and I'll have it in writing. A rewrite for what, though, when you haven't shown me a single page. And under your own procedure its mark replaces the zero, so say that too.
Take it, or I walk out of here right now.
Walk out, and I walk to the principal's office. Or turn the screen.
